selection.user_question:
我负责数据中心共封装光学模块中的硅微光学耦合元件。模块需要兼容 1260-1360 nm 和 1530-1565 nm 两个通信波段，希望采用一套镀膜降低空气与硅界面的反射，减少不同波段单独设计镀膜的复杂度。请为硅元件的入射表面设计平面多层介质减反膜：空气入射、入射角 0 deg、非偏振 unpolarized，硅作为半无限出射基底；在上述两个波段分别尽可能降低平均反射率，并报告进入硅基底的透射率。膜层仅允许 Ta2O5 和 SiO2，总层数不超过 12 层。
单层膜厚（layer thickness）：20-400 nm。
请比较宽带与双波段匹配方案，利用真实光谱结果调整膜厚，给出两波段之间的性能折中及最终结构。评价范围是局部平面界面的功率反射与透射。

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether an 8-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 stack with optimized individual thicknesses can simultaneously suppress reflectance across both O-band (1260-1360 nm) and C-band (1530-1565 nm) on a silicon substrate. The design draws on recalled thin-film interference principles: quarter-wave optical thicknesses create destructive interference, and multiple alternating high/low index layers broaden the bandwidth. I would have wanted to look up exact dispersion data for Ta2O5 and SiO2 in these bands, published dual-band AR designs on silicon, and whether 8 layers is sufficient or if 10-12 would be needed for the two-band requirement.

routes.title: Eight-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 anti-reflection stack with thickness optimization for dual-band operation
routes.scientific_hypothesis: An 8-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 stack with individually optimized thicknesses can achieve average reflectance below 2% in both the 1260-1360 nm and 1530-1565 nm bands simultaneously on a silicon substrate at normal incidence.
routes.design_principle: Recalled thin-film interference theory: quarter-wave optical thicknesses create destructive interference for reflected waves at interfaces. Alternating high-index (Ta2O5) and low-index (SiO2) layers create an impedance-matching gradient from air to silicon. Multiple layer pairs broaden the low-reflectance bandwidth compared to a single quarter-wave layer. Starting with low-index on the air side reduces the first-interface reflection.
routes.proposed_topology: air | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | silicon_substrate
soft_objectives: minimize average reflectance in 1260-1360 nm band
minimize average reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band
balance performance between the two bands rather than favoring one
manufacturing_considerations: all layer thicknesses must be between 20 nm and 400 nm
total layer count is exactly 8 (within the 12-layer maximum)
materials restricted to Ta2O5 and SiO2 as specified
normal incidence deposition assumed for design
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness (n*d = lambda/4) creates destructive interference for normal-incidence reflection at the target wavelength
Alternating high/low index layers create a stepped impedance match from air (n~1) to silicon (n~3.5 in NIR)
More layer pairs generally broaden the anti-reflection bandwidth but increase complexity
Starting with low-index material on the air side reduces the first-interface Fresnel reflection
Dual-band optimization requires thicknesses that are not simple quarter-waves at either band center but compromise values
expected_advantages: Eight layers provide more degrees of freedom than a simple 4-layer quarter-wave stack for dual-band tuning
Alternating structure is manufacturable with standard deposition processes
SiO2 and Ta2O5 are common optical coating materials with good durability
Fixed topology allows clean comparison of thickness optimization effectiveness
known_risks: Ta2O5 is not in the guaranteed_names list (sio2 and si are); name resolution may fail and require repair
Recalled refractive indices are approximate: SiO2 ~1.45, Ta2O5 ~2.1-2.2, Si ~3.5 in NIR; actual dispersion may differ
Eight layers may be insufficient for true dual-band performance; 10-12 layers might be needed but I fixed 8 to keep the axis clean
The trade-off between O-band and C-band performance may favor one band significantly; I do not know the achievable balance from memory
Thickness bounds (20-400 nm) may constrain optimal solutions if quarter-wave thicknesses fall outside this range for these materials and wavelengths
No literature was consulted to verify whether this specific material pair and layer count is conventional for dual-band AR on silicon
routes.execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer anti-reflection coating on a silicon substrate. Incident medium is air. Incidence angle is 0 degrees. Polarization is unpolarized. The stack topology is exactly: air | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | silicon_substrate (8 dielectric layers total, alternating SiO2 (Lemarchand) and Ta2O5 (Gao), starting with SiO2 (Lemarchand) on the air side). Optimize the 8 individual layer thicknesses to minimize average reflectance across two wavelength bands simultaneously: 1260-1360 nm and 1530-1565 nm. Each layer thickness must be between 20 nm and 400 nm. Materials are SiO2 (Lemarchand), Ta2O5 (Gao), and Si (substrate only). Report the optimized thicknesses, the average reflectance in each band, and the transmittance into the silicon substrate. The objective is to balance performance between the two bands rather than minimizing one at the expense of the other.

plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route fails to produce any valid candidates after three revision cycles, the problem may require a different material pair, a different layer count, or the thickness bounds may be too restrictive for the wavelength range. Escalate for manual review rather than continuing to iterate.

expected_observations: best_target_score should increase across iteration rounds as thickness optimization converges
valid_candidates count should remain high (most thickness combinations should be physically valid)
tightest_margin should not systematically decrease across rounds if the optimization is stable
If the hypothesis holds, average reflectance in both bands should be comparable and low; if it fails, one band will show significantly higher reflectance than the other
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates drops below 10 percent of the candidate pool for two consecutive rounds, relax the thickness bounds by 10 nm on each side and continue
if tightest_margin becomes negative for more than half the candidates in a round, reduce the step size for thickness perturbations and continue
